title: My Honest Take on Lavender Tallow Balm for Spring Skin
body:
Okay so it’s spring. The air is doing that thing. It’s not cold, not warm, just… aggressively breezy and sort of damp but also weirdly dry? I was sitting outside yesterday, it was like 73 degrees but the wind was going. My face felt like it was made of paper. That tight, itchy paper feeling. You know the one. Like if you smile too wide your cheek might just crack and flake off. My skin gets so confused this time of year. One minute it’s oily from the humidity, the next it’s a desert. It’s the worst. My knuckles were looking like a topographic map of the moon. Anyway. That’s the whole vibe. Dry spring skin. It’s a thing.

I tried a lot of stuff before this. The expensive stuff in the blue jar from the mall. The drugstore lotion that smells like fake flowers and just sits on top of your skin feeling greasy. I even tried that weird gel stuff that promises to lock in moisture but just makes you feel sticky. Nothing really fixed the paper-face feeling. It all just… managed it. Badly.

Then I kept seeing people talk about tallow. Beef fat. For your face. I was skeptical. Obviously. It sounds like something your great-grandmother might have used, or like a weird TikTok trend. But I was desperate. And curious. So I ordered this whipped tallow balm, the lavender one, from this little Etsy shop. It comes from France, made from grass-fed beef suet they whip into this… texture. I didn’t expect much. Honestly I thought it might be gross.

## How Beef Tallow Ended Up on My Face

The jar showed up. It’s small. I opened it. First thought: it doesn’t look like beef fat. It looks like really thick, pale butter. Or like cool whip that’s been in the fridge too long. I scooped a little. It’s solid but soft. You have to warm it up between your fingers. Which feels weirdly ceremonial. Like you’re preparing a tiny potion. The smell hit me then. Lavender. But not the sharp, cleaning-product lavender. This is… quieter. Like dried lavender in an old linen closet. Or the smell in the air right after it rains on lavender plants. It’s herbal. Calming. It doesn’t scream. It just sits there, being purple-smelling.

I rubbed it on the back of my hand first. Because I wasn’t about to slather unknown beef product on my face immediately. My skin just drank it. Like, it was there, and then it wasn’t. No grease. No shiny film. My hand just felt like my hand, but softer. Not “soft” like a commercial. Just… normal. Hydrated. I was surprised. So I got brave and put a tiny bit on my cheeks and forehead that night.

Here’s the science part I read after, which made the weirdness make sense: tallow is supposed to be really close to the oils our own skin makes. Our sebum. So it absorbs deep instead of sitting on top. It’s good for sensitive skin, dry skin, all that. It sounded logical after the fact. But in the moment, I was just a person rubbing whipped cow fat on my face before bed, hoping for the best.

## What This Lavender Balm Actually Does

My routine now is stupid simple. I wash my face with water. Sometimes a cleanser if I wore makeup, which is like twice a month. Pat it dry. Then I take a little scoop of this tallow balm, warm it up, and just press it into my skin. Mostly at night. The lavender smell is… it’s the best part, maybe. It’s not a perfume. It’s like the scent version of a weighted blanket. My brain just goes “oh. bedtime.” It’s genuinely relaxing. I put it on and my shoulders drop like two inches. I sleep better. I don’t know if it’s the tallow or the ritual or the smell, but the whole thing is this quiet, soothing pause at the end of the day.

This is a tangent but my cat loves the smell. He tries to rub his face on my chin after I put it on. He’s a weirdo.

The results aren’t dramatic in a “transformative glow” way. They’re subtle. But real. That tight, papery feeling I started with? Gone after like three days. My skin just feels… settled. Even. When I wake up, my face doesn’t feel parched. It feels balanced. My knuckles aren’t cracked anymore. I used it on my elbows, which are always rough, and they’re smoother now. Not baby smooth. Just not sandpaper. I’ve even started using a tiny bit under my eyes where I get those little dry lines. They’re less noticeable. Not gone. Just less… pronounced.

I got mine from a shop on Etsy called PureVelvet or something like that. The jar is simple. It feels solid. It’s not fancy packaging, which I kind of like. You’re paying for the stuff inside, not a heavy glass bottle.

## My Skin Now, In This Weird Spring Weather

So it’s been a few weeks. Spring is fully here. The pollen is coating everything in yellow dust. The weather can’t make up its mind. But my skin has. It’s just… fine. It’s not a headline. It’s not “perfect.” It’s just not a problem anymore. I don’t think about it. That’s the biggest win. I don’t have a 12-step routine. I have a one-step routine: tallow balm at night. Sometimes in the morning if it’s extra windy.

I wore a lighter foundation the other day and it didn’t cling to dry patches. Because there aren’t any. That was a weird moment. I looked in the mirror and thought, huh. It just works.

Would I buy it again? I already did. I’m on my second jar. I got one for my mom too, who has skin so sensitive everything makes it red. She texted me last week saying her hands haven’t been this good in years. She uses it like hand cream. So yeah. It’s a keeper.

It’s not magic. It’s not going to make you look 20 again. But if your skin is being difficult with the season change, if you have dry spring skin that nothing seems to fix, this tallow balm for spring might be worth a shot. It’s just a simple thing that does one job really well: it makes your skin feel like skin again. Not a project. Just… your skin.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Yeah, weirdly. From what I understand, it’s similar to the oils our skin already makes. So it gets absorbed deep instead of sitting on top feeling greasy. My face seems to recognize it. It just works with it.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
Hasn’t for me. And I can get clogged pores pretty easy. Because it absorbs so well, it doesn’t just block everything up. It’s the opposite of that heavy lotion feeling.

**What does the lavender tallow balm smell like?**
It’s a real, herbal lavender. Not sweet. Not like air freshener. It’s like crushed dried lavender buds. Earthy and calming. It’s the main reason I use it at night—it just tells my brain to shut off.

Anyway. That’s my experience. If you’re curious about trying something different for your seasonal skincare, might be worth checking out. My skin’s happy, I’m happy. That’s all I wanted.
